proof: tests/models/test_meta_cli_restrictions.py passes without live calls (stubbed subprocess): the probe secret and every unlisted key are stripped from the child environment, the child cwd pins to the allowed root (defaulting to the invoking directory, recorded), the argv names no peer-dispatch capability, the spawn gate refuses MCP/tool/dispatch/peer/delegate flags without spawning (free-text wording never trips it), and last_invocation plus completion meta carry argv/cwd/env-key names/contributor/requested and returned model identity plus requested_permissions separately from observed_permissions with no secret values; tests/models/test_child_capability.py proves the same denials child-side through the real adapter path (17 tests, no live model calls): a real spawned fixture child reports no secret, no RULOOM_* key, and no MCP/tool-routing config -- including a grandchild peer the fixture child dispatches to -- cwd pinned with relative writes contained, the spawn gate refusing tool/dispatch flags before anything spawns on fixture and real muse exec argv shapes, requested vs observed permissions recorded; the pinned directory is NOT filesystem confinement (an absolute write outside the root still lands) so that containment stays claimed only by the planned Q-GOV-TOOL-CONTAINMENT rule; the live child may additionally report interpreter/platform-injected locale keys (LC_CTYPE, __CF_USER_TEXT_ENCODING), named explicitly and audited for secret values; one fake-model tabular run proves the run record stores a model_invocation event per call with role, client, effective invocation, and requested vs observed permissions; HP-03 model identity (12 tests in tests/models/test_model_identity.py, stubbed transport only): requested vs observed stay separate with unknown when the transport supplies none (never a requested fallback), multi-model usage aggregates as multiple:B+C with per-model entries preserved and summed, mismatch never refuses, and the run log records requested, returned, and per-model entries per call (local adapter follows the same unknown-when-silent convention).
title: Restricted model invocation with recorded effective permissions
